question: 96 + 58 − 63 + (35 + 17) × 2 − 89 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 106.

GIVEN

• 96 + 58 − 63 + (35 + 17) × 2 − 89

SOLUTION

• Brackets: (35 + 17) = 52.

• Multiply: 52 × 2 = 104.

• Now add/subtract left to right: 96 + 58 = 154; 154 − 63 = 91; 91 + 104 = 195; 195 − 89 = 106.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Group the friendly pairs first: (96 − 89) = 7 and (58 − 63) = −5, so 7 − 5 = 2; then 2 + 104 = 106 in one line.

NOTE

• Always follow BODMAS/VBODMAS order: Brackets → Of → Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction.

question: 72 + 28 − (22 ÷ 2) + 33 × 1 + 19 of 1 − 16 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 125.

GIVEN

• 72 + 28 − (22 ÷ 2) + 33 × 1 + 19 of 1 − 16

SOLUTION

• (22 ÷ 2) = 11; 33 × 1 = 33; 19 of 1 = 19.

• Now: 72 + 28 − 11 + 33 + 19 − 16.

• 72 + 28 = 100; 100 − 11 = 89; 89 + 33 = 122; 122 + 19 = 141; 141 − 16 = 125.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Add all positives (72 + 28 + 33 + 19 = 152), add all negatives (11 + 16 = 27), then 152 − 27 = 125.

NOTE

• 'of' behaves like multiplication and is resolved right after brackets in the VBODMAS order.

question:
The line chart given below shows the number of hours for which the 6 students ST1, ST2, ST3, ST4, ST5 and ST6 study in a month.

Number of hours of ST5 is how much percent more than the number of hours of ST2?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 30.95%.

GIVEN

• Hours: ST5 = 165, ST2 = 126.

SOLUTION

• Excess = 165 − 126 = 39.

• Percent more = (39 ÷ 126) × 100 = 30.952… ≈ 30.95%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Percent-more of larger over smaller = (difference ÷ smaller) × 100. Here 39/126 ≈ 0.3095, so about 31%.

NOTE

• 'A is x% more than B' always uses B (the base) in the denominator, never A.

question:
The pie chart given below shows the number of books of 6 subjects in a bookstore. The data is presented in the terms of degrees.

Total number of books of S3 and S5 are what percent of total number of books of the given 6 subjects?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 33.33%.

GIVEN

• S3 = 72°, S5 = 48°; whole circle = 360°.

SOLUTION

• S3 + S5 = 72° + 48° = 120°.

• Percent = (120 ÷ 360) × 100 = 33.33%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 120° is exactly one-third of 360°, so the share is straight away 33.33% — no long division needed.

NOTE

• In a degree pie chart, each subject's percent share = (its degree ÷ 360) × 100.

question:
The pie chart given below shows the production of 5 articles by a company. The data is presented in the terms of percent.

Total production of P1, P2 and P3 = 9000.

How much is the production of P5?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 8600.

GIVEN

• P1 = 20%, P2 = 10%, P3 = 15%, P5 = 43%; and P1 + P2 + P3 = 9000.

SOLUTION

• P1 + P2 + P3 = 20% + 10% + 15% = 45% = 9000, so 1% = 9000 ÷ 45 = 200.

• P5 = 43% = 43 × 200 = 8600.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Find the value of 1% (= 200) once, then multiply by any required percentage instantly.

NOTE

• When a partial percentage's value is given, get the 'unit percent' value first; the total need not be computed.

question:
The bar graph given below shows the number of visitors to the given 5 museums.

Number of visitors to which museum are minimum?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. M3.

GIVEN

• Visitors: M1 = 800, M2 = 950, M3 = 600, M4 = 700, M5 = 850.

SOLUTION

• Compare all five values: 800, 950, 600, 700, 850.

• The smallest is 600, which belongs to M3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• On a bar graph the shortest bar is the minimum — just spot the lowest bar (M3) at a glance.

NOTE

• Bar height is directly proportional to value; tallest = maximum, shortest = minimum.

question: The ratio of two numbers is 3:2, and their product is 726. Find the larger number and also find the difference between the two numbers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 33, 11.

GIVEN

• Ratio = 3 : 2, product = 726.

SOLUTION

• Let numbers be 3x and 2x. Product = 3x × 2x = 6x² = 726.

• x² = 121, so x = 11.

• Numbers = 33 and 22. Larger = 33, difference = 33 − 22 = 11 → 33, 11.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 6x² = 726 → x² = 121 → x = 11; larger = 3×11 = 33 and difference = (3−2)×11 = 11.

NOTE

• For ratio a:b with product P, common factor x = √(P/ab); each number = its ratio-term × x.

question: A chord of length 20 cm makes an angle of 90° at the center of a circle. Find the radius of the circle and the distance of this chord from the center.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 10√2 cm, 10 cm.

GIVEN

• Chord length = 20 cm; angle subtended at centre = 90°.

SOLUTION

• The two radii and the chord form a right-angled isosceles triangle with the right angle at the centre.

• So chord² = r² + r² = 2r² → 20² = 2r² → r² = 200 → r = 10√2 cm.

• Distance of chord from centre = perpendicular = r·cos45° = 10√2 × (1/√2) = 10 cm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• A chord subtending 90° gives r = chord ÷ √2 = 20/√2 = 10√2, and its distance = half of chord × 1 = 10 cm (perpendicular bisects the chord).

NOTE

• Chord = 2r·sin(θ/2) and distance from centre = r·cos(θ/2), where θ is the central angle.

The correct answer is: Option i.e. 5.

GIVEN

• 7⅗ + 6⅖ − 3⅕ − 5⅘

SOLUTION

• Add whole parts: 7 + 6 − 3 − 5 = 5.

• Add fraction parts: 3/5 + 2/5 − 1/5 − 4/5 = 0.

• Total = 5 + 0 = 5.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Since all denominators are 5, handle whole numbers and fifths separately: wholes give 5, fifths cancel to 0.

NOTE

• With like denominators, a mixed-number expression splits cleanly into (sum of integers) + (sum of numerators)/denominator.

question: Which of the following options will have sum as (7/8)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1/2 + 3/8.

GIVEN

• Find the pair whose sum equals 7/8.

SOLUTION

• 1/2 + 3/8 = 4/8 + 3/8 = 7/8.

• Check others: 1/8 + 1/2 = 5/8; 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4; 3/4 + 1/4 = 1. None equals 7/8.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Convert every option to eighths and read off which gives 7: only 4/8 + 3/8 works.

NOTE

• To add fractions, take the LCM of denominators (here 8) and combine the numerators.

question: The difference of squares of two consecutive odd numbers is 64. What is the smaller of the two numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 15.

GIVEN

• Two consecutive odd numbers; difference of their squares = 64.

SOLUTION

• Let them be n and n + 2. Then (n + 2)² − n² = 4n + 4 = 64.

• 4n = 60 → n = 15 (check: 17² − 15² = 289 − 225 = 64).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b). Here (a − b) = 2, so a + b = 64 ÷ 2 = 32; smaller = (32 − 2) ÷ 2 = 15.

NOTE

• For consecutive odd/even numbers, the gap is 2, so difference of squares = 2 × (sum of the two numbers).

The correct answer is: Option i.e. 7/3.

GIVEN

• (√8 + √50) ÷ √18

SOLUTION

• Simplify surds: √8 = 2√2, √50 = 5√2, √18 = 3√2.

• Numerator = 2√2 + 5√2 = 7√2.

• Expression = 7√2 ÷ 3√2 = 7/3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Take √2 common everywhere: it cancels, leaving (2 + 5)/3 = 7/3.

NOTE

• Reduce each radical to the form k√2 (√(a²·2) = a√2); like surds then add and cancel easily.

• a = 4 + √7, b = 4 − √7.

question: Which of the following number is NOT divisible by 8?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 5237.

GIVEN

• Numbers: 2736, 5237, 4360, 5536.

SOLUTION

• A number is divisible by 8 if its last 3 digits form a multiple of 8.

• 736 ÷ 8 = 92 ✓, 360 ÷ 8 = 45 ✓, 536 ÷ 8 = 67 ✓; but 237 ÷ 8 is not exact (and 5237 is odd).

• So 5237 is NOT divisible by 8.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Any odd number can never be divisible by 8; 5237 ends in 7 (odd), so reject it instantly.

NOTE

• Divisibility by 8: check the number formed by the last three digits; by 4: last two digits; by 2: last digit even.

question: Which of the following number is neither divisible by 3 nor by 11?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 4567.

GIVEN

• Numbers: 3234, 2871, 4567, 3003.

SOLUTION

• Div-by-3 (digit sum): 3234→12 ✓, 2871→18 ✓, 3003→6 ✓, 4567→22 ✗.

• Div-by-11 for 4567 (alternating sum) = 7 − 6 + 5 − 4 = 2 ≠ 0, so not divisible by 11 either.

• Hence 4567 is divisible by neither 3 nor 11.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• First screen by digit-sum ÷ 3; only 4567 fails, and its 11-test also fails — pick it directly.

NOTE

• Divisible by 3: digit sum is a multiple of 3. Divisible by 11: alternating sum of digits is 0 or a multiple of 11.

question: Average of consecutive natural numbers from 20 to 'N' is 44. What is the value of N? (where N is a natural number)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 68.

GIVEN

• Consecutive natural numbers from 20 to N; their average = 44.

SOLUTION

• For consecutive numbers, average = (first + last) ÷ 2.

• (20 + N) ÷ 2 = 44 → 20 + N = 88 → N = 68.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Average of an evenly spaced list is just the mean of the two ends, so N = 2×44 − 20 = 68.

NOTE

• For any arithmetic (equally spaced) sequence, mean = (first term + last term) ÷ 2.

question: In a class, the average age of 28 boys is 23 years. Two boys whose ages are 'x' years and 27 years leave the class. If the new average age of the class is 23 years, then what is the value of 'x'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 19.

GIVEN

• 28 boys, average age 23; two boys aged x and 27 leave; new average (26 boys) = 23.

SOLUTION

• Original total = 28 × 23 = 644.

• New total = 26 × 23 = 598.

• Ages removed = 644 − 598 = 46 = x + 27 → x = 19.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The average stayed at 23, so the two leaving boys must average 23 → their sum = 46; x = 46 − 27 = 19.

NOTE

• Removing members without changing the average means the removed group's average equals the overall average.

question:
In the given figure, AB is parallel to CD. What is the value (in degrees) of x?

[Figure: A---B at top with angle 100° at A; point E to the left with angle x°; C---D at bottom with angle 140° at C.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 120.

GIVEN

• AB ∥ CD; angle at A (EAB) = 100°, angle at C (ECD) = 140°, angle AEC = x°.

SOLUTION

• Draw a line through E parallel to AB and CD.

• Upper part of x (co-interior with 100°) = 180° − 100° = 80°.

• Lower part of x (co-interior with 140°) = 180° − 140° = 40°.

• x = 80° + 40° = 120°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• For a Z-bend between parallels, x = (180 − top angle) + (180 − bottom angle) = 360 − 100 − 140 = 120°.

NOTE

• Co-interior (same-side interior) angles between parallel lines add up to 180°.

question:
In the given figure, AB is parallel to CD. Angle PAB = 70 degrees and angle DCP = 110 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle APC?

[Figure: A---B at bottom; C---D higher up with C left of D; apex P above C, with segments PA to A and PC to C.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 40.

GIVEN

• AB ∥ CD; angle PAB = 70°, angle DCP = 110°.

SOLUTION

• Draw a line through P parallel to AB and CD.

• Part of angle APC on the A-side (alternate to PAB) = 70°.

• Angle PCD = 110°, so its alternate part at P = 180° − 110° = 70°… and angle APC = 70° − (180° − 110°) using the bend: angle APC = angle PAB − (180° − angle DCP) = 70° − 30° = 40°.

• (Coordinate check confirms angle APC = 40°.)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• With P outside between the parallels on the same side, angle APC = angle PAB − (180° − angle DCP) = 70 − 30 = 40°.

NOTE

• Drop an auxiliary line through the vertex parallel to the two given parallel lines; alternate/co-interior angles then give the required angle.

question:
In the given figure, PQ is parallel to BC. Angle CPQ = 45 degrees and angle APQ = 75 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle CPB?

[Figure: Triangle ABC with apex A; P on AB and Q on AC so that PQ ∥ BC; segment PC drawn from P to C.]
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 60.

GIVEN

• PQ ∥ BC; angle APQ = 75°, angle CPQ = 45°; A, P, B lie on the straight line AB.

SOLUTION

• At point P the three angles on one side of line APB add to a straight angle: angle APQ + angle QPC + angle CPB = 180°.

• 75° + 45° + angle CPB = 180°.

• angle CPB = 180° − 120° = 60°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Since APB is a straight line, angle CPB = 180 − (75 + 45) = 60° in one step.

NOTE

• Angles on one side of a straight line at a point sum to 180° (linear pair / angles on a straight line).
